newsitem.title: USA: BankWatch ups El Salvador/Guatemala risk ratings.
newsitem.headline: BankWatch ups El Salvador/Guatemala risk ratings.

text.p: Thomson BankWatch said on Monday it raised the sovereign risk ratings of Guatemala and El Salvador.

The bank rating agency said it upgraded Guatemala's soverign risk rating to B-minus from single-C based on the country's improved political stability and economic prospects resulting from the recent peace treaty between the Guatemalan government and the left-wing Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unity.
The accord, which was signed on December 29, 1996, brings an end to Central America's last and longest-running civil war, the agency added.

Guatemala's new-found peace, however, makes fiscal reform all the more critical, the agency said. Constrained by one of the lowest tax collection rates in the region, Guatemala continues to face fiscal financing pressures which could threaten the postwar economic recovery.
While recent government measures aimed at raising tax revenues should help along these lines, further efforts will be necessary to get the country's fiscal house in order, BankWatch said.
BankWatch also upgraded the sovereign risk rating of El Salvador to BB-minus from B-minus citing the country's improved economic performance and continued politcal stability.

Broad-based popular support for the government's economic policies has enabled a deepening of the reform process. Extensive economic liberalization, including the elimination of interest rate, capital and price controls, have bolstered the prospects for a sustained economic expansion, the agency said.
At the same time, BankWatch added, prudent monetary and fiscal policies have helped reduce budgetary and inflationary pressures, despite the high costs associated with the peace accords.
